title: Clavicula Salomonis Regis
shelf_note: An 18th-century manuscript Key of Solomon (Penn Colenda); core grimoire material for a library of the magical and Hermetic tradition. No tradition or collection is assigned.
structure_note: 245 pages, all with OCR, 228 translated. Page 58 and page 184 are in visibly different hands (a formal italic cursive with a ruled red margin; a looser cursive), so this may be a composite manuscript or written by more than one scribe. Page 122 is a pasted-in blank blue paper roundel (a pentacle that was never filled in), with show-through from the verso below it.

ocr_errors.image: '43' written in the left margin beside the prayer 'Adonaij Potentissime', not at the head of the page
ocr_errors.problem: a marginal number (probably numbering the prayer or a section) is tagged as the page number
scribal spelling silently normalised

tr_errors.english: an earthen vessel capable of holding <note>coals</note>, full of coals
tr_errors.problem: redundant inline note: 'Capax' just means 'capacious'

other.note: <note> tags appear inline in the reader translation ('<note>coals</note>', '<note>mercy</note>')

ocr_errors.ocr: Below the diagram, there are traces of very faint, illegible handwritten text, likely in Latin, which has faded significantly over time.
ocr_errors.image: the faint lines below the roundel are show-through from the verso (reversed writing), not faded text on this page
ocr_errors.problem: show-through from the other side of the leaf is described as faded text on this page

ocr_errors.ocr: A circular diagram or seal, lightly drawn or faded ... faint geometric or sigillic markings
ocr_errors.image: a pasted-on pale blue paper disc, essentially blank apart from a few pen strokes and an ink smear, set in a faint ruled pencil square
ocr_errors.problem: an unfinished pasted roundel is described as a faded talismanic seal

tr_errors.source: <image-desc>…</image-desc> <unclear>…</unclear>
tr_errors.english: <note>A circular diagram or seal…</note> <unclear>…</unclear> <summary>This page contains a faded and largely illegible talismanic diagram, consistent with the protective seals found elsewhere in the manuscript.</summary>
tr_errors.problem: the translation pane carries a page description in place of a translation, and the summary claims the leaf is a faded seal like others in the manuscript, which the image does not show

other.note: Raw <note>, <unclear>, <summary> and <keywords> tags make up the whole translation of a near-blank plate
<summary> and <keywords> tags at the end of the reader translation

book_verdict: The transcription of the text pages is very good and so are the translations. The defect is the plate leaf (p.122): a blank pasted roundel comes out as a 'faded talismanic seal', faded text that is really show-through, and a translation pane made of tags.

title: Carmina congratulatoria. In honorem ... D. Adami myriciani chrimnicensis ...
shelf_note: A 1565 Ingolstadt pamphlet of occasional verse congratulating a new doctor of medicine. It is genuine period humanist material and touches on medicine (Machaon, Hippocrates, Galen), but sits outside the library's core esoteric and early-science traditions. No tradition or collection is assigned.
structure_note: 16 pages, 14 translated, which fits a short pamphlet with blank or title leaves. Signatures A3 (p.5), B (p.9) and Biij (p.13) run in order.

ocr_errors.problem: a printed page is tagged as handwritten
long s read as f, giving a non-word ('Deferuit' for 'Deseruit'); the translation still renders 'abandoned'

tr_errors.source: Hic igitur primum de Bacca nomine lauri / Pro studij fructu ... potitus / Ritè creabatur dicebaturque Magister
tr_errors.english: Here, therefore, first, from the berry of the laurel / He was duly created and called Master, having obtained / The fruit of study
tr_errors.problem: the lines first record the baccalaureate (the 'name from the laurel berry') and then the master's degree; the translation merges them, so the bachelor's degree is lost

tr_errors.source: Vt uel in Hippocratis libris, uel in arte Galeni,
tr_errors.english: As if in the books of Hippocrates, or in the art of Galen,
tr_errors.problem: 'Ut vel … vel' means 'so that, whether in … or in …', not 'as if'

ocr_errors.ocr: Ac seruare datam caelestum munere uitam
ocr_errors.problem: œ and circumflex normalised

tr_errors.source: Atque salutarem captabant numinis auram.
tr_errors.english: And they sought the healthy air of his divinity.
tr_errors.problem: 'salutarem auram' is the saving or healing breath of the godhead; 'healthy air' is flat and misleading

tr_errors.source: Nec uanus quisque facilè id persuaserit author,
tr_errors.english: And no vain author could easily persuade one that,
tr_errors.problem: the line carries on to the next page; the rendering is awkward and leaves the sense unclear

tr_errors.source: Chrimnicensis
tr_errors.english: of Chrimnicz
tr_errors.problem: inconsistent with 'Crimnitz' on p.5; the place is Chemnitz

other.note: The woodcut-initial description is wrapped in a <meta> tag inside the reader translation

book_verdict: A clean, faithful reading of a short printed congratulatory pamphlet. The only blemishes are a wrong 'handwritten' tag on a printed page and one couplet where the bachelor's degree is lost in translation.

title: Contra Celsum (1481 editio princeps)
shelf_note: Origen against Celsus, Latin translation by Persona, Rome: Herolt 1481. It is a core text for late-antique polemic over pagan philosophy and Christianity, including the Platonist views of soul and daemons.
structure_note: 538 pages, all with OCR, 524 translated, which is consistent. Nothing stands out.

ocr_errors.ocr: Erat igitur iſtiuſmodi Ieſus ut Celſus exiſtimat
ocr_errors.problem: 'uti' read as 'ut'

tr_errors.source: nisi dementibus & freneſi laborantibus: uel furentibus
tr_errors.english: except to those suffering from madness, frenzy, or madness
tr_errors.problem: the three terms (the demented, the frenzied, the raving) collapse into a repeated 'madness'

other.note: Translation opens with '<meta>Continuity: Continues the defense of the resurrection …</meta>', which is model apparatus visible in the reader text

tr_errors.source: …apertius que ſupradicta ſunt demonſtrabimus: quis autem qui moderatior ſit … non huius comprimat impudentiam … brutorum animantium cauſa: ut condita fuerint hec omnia demõſtrare.
tr_errors.english: "… we will demonstrate more openly what was said above. For who, being more moderate … would not suppress the impudence of this man … to demonstrate that all these things were founded not more for the sake of men than for brute animals."
tr_errors.problem: the quotation mark for Celsus's words is closed only after Origen's own rebuttal, so Origen's attack on Celsus's 'impudence' reads as Celsus speaking

tr_errors.source: earum rerum inſimulent: in quibus ſibi amantiſſimi quidam collaudantur
tr_errors.english: of those things in which they themselves are highly praised by their most loving friends
tr_errors.problem: the sense is 'things for which some of those dearest to them are praised'; the translation makes the accusers the ones praised

tr_errors.source: nihil aduertit uel Stoicos ſe philoſophos criminari
tr_errors.english: notices nothing, or that he is criticizing Stoic philosophers
tr_errors.problem: 'vel' means 'even' here: he does not notice that he is even accusing the Stoics. Rendered as 'or', which garbles the point

ocr_errors.image: cūqȝ ea puelit dicta p bare
ocr_errors.problem: an abbreviation mark is dropped or regularised ('puelit')

tr_errors.source: quia inter ſe nihil conſtituant & filios ſinant ſe debellare
tr_errors.english: because they determine nothing among themselves and allow their sons to destroy them
tr_errors.problem: 'sinant [filios] se debellare' means 'let the sons fight it out among themselves', not 'destroy them [the parents]'

tr_errors.source: si diuinus ierat et in corpore ſpiritus
tr_errors.english: if He was divine and the spirit was in a body
tr_errors.problem: the sense is 'if a divine spirit was in a body'

book_verdict: The incunable is transcribed accurately and the translations are mostly faithful. There are a few moderate slips in the hard Latin of the polemic, including one misplaced quotation mark on p.270 that puts Origen's rebuttal in Celsus's mouth.

title: Carmen elegia gratulatoria in honorem et gratiam Martini Fabricii zuellichiensis ...
shelf_note: A 1583 Frankfurt-an-der-Oder congratulatory elegy for a master's degree. It is minor occasional humanist verse, outside the core esoteric and early-science traditions. No tradition or collection is assigned.
structure_note: Pages 9 and 13 are not part of the 1583 elegy. They are leaves of a later handwritten index to the composite volume the pamphlet was bound into: numbered entries 89–106 and 161–173 for congratulatory prints dated 1588–1610. The printed elegy only begins around p.19 (signature A2). Readers who open 'Elegia gratulatoria 1583' meet manuscript lists of 1599–1610 prints first. 29 pages, 19 translated.

ocr_errors.problem: the author's forename 'Tob.' (Tobias, cf. entry 102 'Tobiae Sculteti') is read as Johannes; the translation repeats 'by Johannes Scultetus'
every abbreviation ('Joh.', 'Andr.', 'Lips.', 'franc.', 'ab amic.') is silently expanded, so the transcription is not what the page shows
the initial looks like I/T, not F (probably Caleb Trygophorus of Frankfurt); I am not certain at this resolution

tr_errors.source: Eorundem — a Johanne Sculteto
tr_errors.english: The same — by Johannes Scultetus
tr_errors.problem: carries the OCR forename error

other.note: <summary> calls the list a 'Register of academic acknowledgments and student collective publications'. It is an index of congratulatory prints bound in the volume. Raw <summary>/<keywords> tags are shown in the reader text.

ocr_errors.problem: æ ligature read as 'oi'
silent expansion of abbreviations

tr_errors.source: Johannis Jacobi Greissen — fautoribus & amicis
tr_errors.english: to patrons and friends
tr_errors.problem: the entry means '[written] by patrons and friends', not 'to' them

tr_errors.source: Christophori Henscheri — gratia amicis (image: grat. amic.)
tr_errors.english: thanks to friends
tr_errors.problem: 'grat. amic.' is the friends' congratulation (gratulatio), not 'thanks to friends'

tr_errors.source: Vinea vite carens
tr_errors.english: A vine lacking grapes
tr_errors.problem: it is a vineyard lacking vines

other.note: OCR carries literal ' ' entities for the pentameter indent, which may show as text in the reader

book_verdict: The printed elegy (p.19) is read and translated very well. The record opens with leaves of a later manuscript index to the bound volume (1588–1610 entries), which a reader would take for part of the 1583 pamphlet, and one name in that list is misread.

title: M. T. Ciceronis officiorum ad Marcum Ciceronem filium
shelf_note: A 15th-century Italian humanist manuscript of Cicero's De officiis (Harvard), with rubricated marginal summaries and illuminated white-vine initials. A classical text; a reasonable shelf for a library of the early modern learned tradition.
structure_note: 274 pages, 272 with OCR, 265 translated. The red running-head letter ('I' on p.67, 'L' on pp.134 and 200) is tagged <page-num> on two pages and <header> on the third, an inconsistent convention; it is not a printed page number.

ocr_errors.problem: 'Parve' read as 'Parvis' in the rubricated margin note

ocr_errors.image: a red running-head 'I' with a cross-stroke above, not a page number
ocr_errors.problem: running head tagged as the page number

other.note: <page-num>, <meta>, <term>/<gloss> and <summary>/<keywords> tags are visible in the reader translation

markdown bold spans invented to mark red initials, covering whole phrases

tr_errors.source: ut proxime trium, saepe multorum clades imperatorum: ut nuper summi ac singularis viri; invidiae praeterea multitudinis
tr_errors.english: as recently the slaughter of three many commanders, as lately the invidiousness of the highest and singular man, furthermore of the multitude
tr_errors.problem: the sense is 'as lately of three [armies], often the defeats of many commanders; as recently [the fall] of one supreme man; besides, the hostility of the multitude'. The translation runs the clauses together into nonsense and ties the 'invidia' to the great man

tr_errors.english: <meta>catchword: speech</meta>
tr_errors.problem: catchword translated

other.note: <header>, <margin>, <meta>, <summary> tags visible in the reader translation

ocr_errors.ocr: Turpe inter honestum et utile facta comparationem
ocr_errors.image: Turpe inter honestum et utile facere comparationem (faded rubric)
ocr_errors.problem: 'facere' read as 'facta'; the translation's 'Shameful comparison' loses 'it is shameful to make'

tr_errors.source: hoc ipsum sensisse quod dixerit solere modo non oportere etiam
tr_errors.english: felt the same thing—that they should not just be accustomed to it, but that it is not even fitting

other.note: <margin> blocks inserted mid-sentence in the translation ('to kill not / <margin>… / only a man')

book_verdict: A well-read humanist manuscript of De officiis with accurate main text and decent translation. Page 134's margin turns Sextus Pompey into 'six', and the clauses about the destroyed armies are run together in translation.
